otu0: What does research with activity trackers show?
otu1: In a 2020 meta-analysis pooling data from more than 44,000 middle-aged and older adults who wore activity trackers, about 30–40 minutes a day of moderate or vigorous activity reduced the higher risk of death linked with long sitting; this is less than earlier estimates based on people’s own reports. In its 2020 guidelines, the World Health Organization also recommends cutting down sitting time and replacing it with activity of any intensity, and advises people who sit a lot to aim above the recommended amount of activity.
